answer: Idle-Span Accrual Gate. Each agent must accumulate a minimum span of idle-then-active timing before its requests gain throughput. A sonnet of intervals: the gate records inter-arrival gaps and rewards regular, human-paced cadence; bursts of clones compress gaps and get throttled. Attacker cost is real wall-clock time plus the umber of parallel sessions held open—each duplicate needs its own slow warmup, and the pearl of throughput comes only after sustained, non-compressed traffic. Dupes must idle at scale, so N identities cost N× the wait and N× the held sessions.
